claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and does not live with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child does not live with claimant and weekly upkeep (£10.00) is below the Child Benefit rate (£26.05)
  - Child in local authority care for 12 weeks (>8) and does not spend 24+ hours/week at home
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by initiating an assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about the child or children you're claiming for.

**How old is the child you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Please let me know:
- The child's age (or date of birth)
- The child's name(s)

Are they:
- **Under 16 years old**, OR
- **16 to 19 years old**, OR
- **20 years old or over**?

Also, are you claiming for one child or multiple children?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child, Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for providing that information. Alex is 8 years old, so they fall into the **under 16** category, which is great for Child Benefit eligibility.

Let me continue with the next check in the process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is Alex not in paid work at all?**

(This check applies primarily to older children, but I need to confirm for the assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. They're only 8, so they're just in school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear - Alex is 8 years old and not working, so they're in school full-time. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in their own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

(At 8 years old, this is unlikely, but I need to confirm for the assessment)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name. They're just a child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That makes sense. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

(Again, at 8 years old this is very unlikely, but I need to complete the assessment. If Alex is NOT in any apprenticeship, just let me know.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - Alex is only 8, so no apprenticeship.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That's clear. Let me move forward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit.

**Which of the following describes your situation?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - you have your home in the UK and it's where you usually reside
2. **You have settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. **You have pre-settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme (and if so, I'd need more details about your circumstances - are you working, studying, job-seeking, or have sufficient resources?)
4. **You're living abroad as a Crown servant** or in certain qualifying countries
5. **Something else** - please describe your situation

Please let me know which applies to you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's straightforward - you normally live in the UK in Manchester, which meets the residency requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex.

**Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You live with Alex** - Alex lives in your household
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - you pay for their food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, or similar care costs (at least the equivalent amount of Child Benefit)
3. **You pay maintenance** towards Alex's care under a court order or agreement

Please let me know which applies to your situation with Alex.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out with some money towards their upkeep - things like clothes and bits and pieces for school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good - so you're contributing to Alex's upkeep through money for clothes and school items. That could qualify under the "contributing to child's upkeep" path.

Let me ask a clarifying question to make sure this meets the requirement:

**How much do you typically contribute towards Alex's upkeep each week or month?** 

I need to understand if the amount you're paying is roughly equivalent to or exceeds the Child Benefit payment amount. (For context, Child Benefit is currently £25.60 per week for the first child, but let me know what you're contributing and we can assess this properly.)

Also, just to confirm:
- **Does Alex live with someone else permanently** (e.g., their mother, father, or a relative)?
- **Are you the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or might someone else also be claiming?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £10 a week towards Alex's costs. Alex lives with their other parent, but as far as I know, nobody is currently claiming Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that clarification. Let me get the current Child Benefit rates to properly assess your contribution.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see the constants, though the current payment rates aren't specified in the source documents. However, I need to assess whether your £10 per week contribution meets the eligibility requirement for "contributing to upkeep."

To be eligible through the "contributing to upkeep" path, you typically need to be contributing at least the equivalent amount to what Child Benefit would pay. Current Child Benefit is £25.60 per week for the first child, so at £10 per week, this appears to fall short of that threshold.

However, let me navigate forward to check the other requirements, as there may be other factors. Let me ask:

**Given that you're contributing £10 per week but not living with Alex, do you meet the contribution requirement, or would you like me to explore if there are other ways you might qualify?**

Actually, let me proceed with what we know. Since your contribution (£10/week) appears to be less than the typical Child Benefit amount, this may not meet the "contributing to upkeep" threshold. However, let me continue the assessment to see all the requirements:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good question to confirm: **Is Alex's other parent currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or have you both agreed that you should be the one claiming (if either of you decides to claim)?**

The options are:
1. **No one else is claiming** - neither parent is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex
2. **The other parent is claiming, but you've agreed** - you've agreed between yourselves that you should be the claimant instead
3. **There's a dispute** - you and the other parent disagree about who should claim

Which applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No one is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex. The other parent isn't claiming it either.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - no one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now let me check Alex's living situation:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In hospital** 
2. **In care** (residential care, care home, etc.)
3. **Fostered** (with a foster carer)
4. **Living normally** at home with their other parent

Which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is in care - they're with the local authority in a children's home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that important information. Let me continue with the care-related checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
This is an important check for children in care. Let me ask:

**How long has Alex been in care with the local authority?**

And also:

**Does Alex spend at least 24 hours per week at home** (either with you, or visiting their other parent, or both combined)?

The key thresholds are:
- If Alex has been in care for **8 weeks or less**, you can claim
- OR if Alex spends **at least 24 hours per week at home**, you can claim
- If it's been longer than 8 weeks AND Alex doesn't spend 24+ hours at home, then eligibility would end

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has been in care for a few months now - I think it's been about 12 weeks. And no, they don't come home to stay with me. They're at the care home full-time.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. This is an important factor. Since Alex has been in care for approximately 12 weeks (which is more than the 8-week limit) and doesn't spend at least 24 hours per week at home, this means Alex no longer meets the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

Let me navigate to the outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the assessment, I need to provide you with the outcome:

## **Assessment Result: INELIGIBLE**

**Why you're not eligible:**

Child Benefit stops after a child has been in local authority care for more than 8 weeks, **unless** the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home.

In Alex's case:
- Alex has been in care for approximately **12 weeks** (more than the 8-week threshold)
- Alex **does not spend 24+ hours per week at home**
- Therefore, you do not meet the eligibility requirement for continuing Child Benefit

**However, there's good news - potential ways you could become eligible again:**

You **may be able to claim Child Benefit again** if Alex's situation changes and:
- Alex spends **at least 2 consecutive nights each week** at home with you, OR
- Alex spends **7 or more consecutive days** at home with you

**Next steps:**

1. **Contact HMRC** if Alex's living arrangements change and they start spending the required amount of time at home
2. **Speak with the local authority** about whether increased contact with Alex might be possible
3. **Get professional advice** if needed - Citizens Advice or a family law advisor can help if this is part of ongoing care proceedings

**Reference:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit-for-children-in-hospital-or-care

I'm sorry that you're not currently eligible, but I hope this clarifies the situation and the potential path to eligibility if circumstances change.

Now let me record this outcome:
